CloseYearRequest.description:
Close the fiscal year containing this date (LED-12).

A date rather than a year, because a fiscal year is named by the calendar year its end
falls in and the entity decides where that boundary sits.

account_type.description: Fixed at creation and never changed (LED-02).
account_type.title: Account Type

retained_earnings.description: Name this account as the one a fiscal year closes to (LED-12). Equity accounts only.
retained_earnings.title: Retained Earnings

CreateEntityRequest.description:
Everything an entity declares at creation, all of it required.

`LED-14` and `LED-15` say the basis, the fiscal year end and the functional currency have
no undeclared state, and `PLT-08` says the same for the time zone. There are no defaults
here for that reason: a default would be an undeclared state wearing a value.

accounting_basis.description: Fixes what every report defaults to. A property of the entity, not a per-report option, and never a posting rule (ADR-0037).
accounting_basis.title: Accounting Basis

functional_currency.description: Amounts in any other commodity are refused until LED-16 activates.
functional_currency.title: Functional Currency

owner.description: The entity's first owner. Defaults to the creating principal; an entity never exists without one (IAM-05).
owner.title: Owner

slug.description: Stable identifier, unique in this deployment.
slug.title: Slug

time_zone.description: Period boundaries are determined in it (PLT-08).
time_zone.title: Time Zone

CreateEntityRequest.title: CreateEntityRequest

ErrorResponse.description:
Every error, on both adapters, in this shape.

`code` is the contract; `message` is not and may be reworded at will (ADR-0015).
ErrorResponse.title: ErrorResponse

GrantRoleRequest.description: Grant a role in this entity. Administrative only (IAM-03).

lapses_at.description: When the role lapses without anyone acting (IAM-09). Null is open-ended.
lapses_at.title: Lapses At

role.description: A role name from this deployment's catalogue. Roles are rows rather than a fixed enumeration, so the set is not enumerable here; an unknown name is refused with `unknown_role` (ADR-0039).
role.title: Role

transaction_date.description: When the event economically occurred. Not when it was recorded — that is server-assigned and cannot be supplied.

ReopenPeriodRequest.description:
Reopen a closed period (LED-11, ADR-0030).

A person's act, never a skill's. `reason` is required: SOC1-17 asks the reopen to capture
one, and a reopen without a reason is indistinguishable from a mistake afterwards.
ReopenPeriodRequest.title: ReopenPeriodRequest

TransactionResponse.description: A transaction as the books hold it.
TransactionResponse.title: TransactionResponse

replayed.description: True when this request replayed an earlier one with the same idempotency key. Nothing was booked a second time.
replayed.title: Replayed

reversed_transaction_ids.description: Stale closing entries reversed by this run (ADR-0027). Empty for a first close.
reversed_transaction_ids.title: Reversed Transaction Ids

post.summary: Create an entity and assign its first owner

post.summary: Add an account to the chart

delete.description:
Revoking is `DELETE` on the route and an update in the schema.

The grant row is never removed — `IAM-14` has to be able to report what was held before
it ended — so the verb describes the effect on access rather than on storage.

post.description: Signifies the period has been reviewed. An agent may do this.

A person's act. An agent is refused with `not_a_person`, whatever it holds.

`POST` rather than `DELETE` on the close: the close row is never removed, and the
reopening is itself a recorded event that `LED-11` requires to be identifiable.

Record a transaction as a draft, or post it straight through.

Requires an `Idempotency-Key` header. Replaying one returns the original result and
books nothing further (ADR-0029).

get.description:
Read a transaction and its postings.

A transaction belonging to another entity is reported as not found rather than as
forbidden: row-level security makes absent and invisible the same answer, and
distinguishing them would leak the other entity's existence (`NFR-04`).

post.description: Move a draft to posted. The point of no return (`LED-07`).

Correct a posted transaction by reversing it, leaving both visible (`LED-08`).

There is deliberately no endpoint that edits or deletes a posted transaction. The
schema refuses both, and offering the route would be offering a way to find out.

Where the reversal lands follows ADR-0030 rule 4 and is decided by the ledger from
the original's period state, not by this adapter: an open original period is restated
in place, and a closed one is corrected in the current period so figures already
reported stand.

Income and expense to retained earnings, so the new year opens at zero (`LED-12`).

Re-runs a close that a later posting made stale, reversing the old entries rather than
editing them (ADR-0027, `LED-08`). A close that is still current is refused.

get.description:
Liveness only. Deliberately touches nothing.

If this checked the database, a database blip would restart every healthy
container — turning a recoverable outage into a rolling one.

Database reachable, and migrations current.

Returns 503 when not ready, so a rollout stops rather than serving traffic
against a schema older than the code.
